title: Mitigating Controls and Techniques

header.html: 4.1 Given a scenario, apply mitigating controls, techniques, and solutions to secure the environment
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

toc.title: Detection and prevention systems and firewalls
Content, endpoint and network access controls

html:
1Overview of the toolbox

Technique Purpose
Segmentation Split the network into zones so an attacker cannot move freely
Access controls Allow only the right users and devices (module 15)
Hardening Remove what is not needed, apply secure settings, patch, change defaults
Sandboxing Run code in an isolated environment to study or limit it
Monitoring and alerting Detect problems quickly (module 14)
Mobile device management (MDM) Enroll, configure and wipe phones and tablets
Application control Allow lists (only approved apps run) or block lists (known bad apps are blocked)
Exam tip

. Allow list = deny everything except what is approved (stronger). Block list = allow everything except what is listed (weaker). Hardening = reduce the attack surface.

2Deception and disruption technology

Tool Meaning
Honeypot A decoy system that attracts attackers
Honeynet A network of honeypots
Honeyfile A fake file that raises an alert when opened
Honeytoken Fake data or credentials that raise an alert when used
Canary account A fake account that alerts when someone tries to use it

They give early warning and reveal attacker methods.

3Detection and prevention systems and firewalls

Item Meaning
IDS Detects and alerts
IPS Detects and blocks
NIDS / NIPS Network-based sensor on the network
HIDS / HIPS Host-based, on one computer
WIPS Wireless intrusion prevention (rogue access points)
Firewall Filters traffic by rules; layer 4 (ports, protocols) or layer 7 (application content)
Rate limiting Caps requests per time to slow floods and brute force
WAF Web application firewall protects web apps from injection and cross-site scripting
Rule-based Traffic matched against ordered rules; ends with an implicit deny
UTM Unified threat management: firewall plus IPS, filtering and antivirus in one device
Exam tip

. IPS blocks, IDS only alerts. A WAF protects web applications at layer 7. A UTM combines several functions in one appliance.

4Content, endpoint and network access controls

Item Meaning
Content filter Blocks bad sites and content
Data loss prevention (DLP) Stops sensitive data leaving; agent-based (on the endpoint) or via a centralized proxy
EDR Endpoint detection and response: records endpoint behavior, detects, isolates and remediates
XDR Extended detection and response: combines endpoint, network, email and cloud signals
Antivirus Detects known malware by signatures and behavior
Network access control (NAC) Decides who may connect; captive portals (a sign-in page), 802.1X (port-based authentication), endpoint posture checks

5Applications, email and operating systems

Area Controls
Repositories Secrets scanning finds keys and passwords in code
Application security Input validation, secure cookies, static code analysis, code signing
Email security SPF (which servers may send for a domain), DKIM (signs messages), DMARC (policy and reporting using SPF and DKIM), BIMI (shows a verified brand logo)
Operating system security Group Policy (central Windows settings), SELinux (mandatory access control on Linux)

Exam tip

. SPF lists allowed sending servers; DKIM gives a signature; DMARC tells receivers what to do when SPF or DKIM fail and sends reports. Code signing proves who wrote code and that it is unchanged.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants only approved programs to run on kiosk computers. Which control fits best?

  • AA block list of known malware
  • BA honeypot
  • CAn application allow list
  • DA captive portal
Show the answer

Answer: C. An allow list permits only approved applications, which is stronger than blocking known bad ones.

S2A fake database account has no real use, and any sign-in attempt on it triggers an alert. What is it?

  • AService account
  • BEmergency access account
  • CCanary account
  • DGuest account
Show the answer

Answer: C. A canary account is a decoy that alerts when anyone tries to use it.

S3Which device both detects malicious traffic and blocks it automatically on the network?

  • ANIPS
  • BNIDS
  • CSIEM
  • DPacket analyzer
Show the answer

Answer: A. A network-based intrusion prevention system detects and blocks, while an IDS only alerts.

S4A web shop wants to filter SQL injection attempts at the application layer. Which control fits?

  • ALayer 4 packet filter
  • BAntivirus
  • CWAF
  • DHoneyfile
Show the answer

Answer: C. A web application firewall inspects layer 7 web traffic for injection and similar attacks.

S5A domain owner wants receivers to reject mail that fails SPF and DKIM checks and to receive reports. Which record does this?

  • ABIMI
  • BCNAME
  • CMX
  • DDMARC
Show the answer

Answer: D. DMARC sets the policy for failed checks and provides reporting.

S6A tool records process activity on laptops, detects suspicious behavior and can isolate a laptop. Which solution is this?

  • AEDR
  • BWAF
  • CMDM
  • DNAC
Show the answer

Answer: A. Endpoint detection and response monitors endpoints and can contain compromised ones.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is hardening?

Show the answer

Reducing the attack surface by removing unneeded features and applying secure settings.

R2What is the difference between a honeypot and a honeytoken?

Show the answer

A honeypot is a decoy system; a honeytoken is fake data or credentials that alert when used.

R3What do SPF, DKIM and DMARC do?

Show the answer

SPF lists allowed senders, DKIM signs messages, DMARC sets policy and reporting.

R4What does 802.1X provide?

Show the answer

Port-based network access authentication.

R5What does XDR add to EDR?

Show the answer

Correlation across endpoint, network, email and cloud signals.

R6What does secrets scanning find?

Show the answer

Keys, tokens and passwords stored in code repositories.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Basics segmentation, access control, hardening, sandboxing, MDM, allow lists (strong) and block lists
Deception honeypot, honeynet, honeyfile, honeytoken, canary account
Detection and filtering IDS alerts, IPS blocks; NIDS/NIPS, HIDS/HIPS, WIPS; firewalls (layer 4 and 7), WAF, rate limiting, UTM
Endpoint and access DLP, EDR, XDR, antivirus; NAC (captive portal, 802.1X, posture)
Apps, email, OS secrets scanning, input validation, secure cookies, static analysis, code signing; SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI; Group Policy, SELinux
